correctness.rationale: Starting from the source reparameterization ell=2 arccos sqrt(1-2L), one has L=(1-cos ell)/4 and the optimum L=1/4 at ell=pi/2. The source gives Q(ell)=4(2pi)^(1/3)(sin ell-ell cos ell)/(3 sin ell+(1/3)sin(3ell)-4ell cos ell)^(2/3). Direct Taylor expansion at ell=pi/2 yields normalized coefficients (pi^2-8)/16 and pi(48-5pi^2)/96 in u=ell-pi/2. Since d=L-1/4=sin(u)/4, u=4d+(32/3)d^3+O(d^5), giving the claimed d-expansion exactly. The packaged symbolic checker verifies these identities and signs from the source formula. No finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source singles out S_{1/4} as the unique rotational minimizer inside the complete classified family of constrained critical surfaces and devotes substantial analysis to stability, but leaves its quotient minimum only qualitative. The exact Hessian supplies the natural local stability modulus of this moduli problem, while the cubic term shows the minimum is directionally skew rather than locally symmetric. This calibrates how the newly discovered critical family departs from its distinguished optimizer and separates scalar moduli stability of the Minkowski quotient from the paper's geometric second-variation stability of the penalized functional.
